tasks.title: Not a Harness Vision
tasks.goal: Define a lightweight, reliability-first native local and SSH terminal workspace whose sessions outlive its desktop UI without becoming an agent harness or runtime.

checks.text: Keep PTYs, child processes, session state, and layouts in a separate Rust service.
Make the native desktop UI a reconnectable client.
Preserve workspaces, sidebar, tabs, split panes, drag-to-rearrange panes, and configured-host SSH workspaces in the product direction.
Reuse an established terminal engine rather than implementing VT behavior.
Defer browser, mobile, generic remote-control UI, worktree/diff, AI integrations, and optional remote-rmuxd reattachment.
Treat terminals and agents as ordinary shell workloads; Not a Harness must stay out of their way rather than own or supervise an agent runtime.
Make bounded history, change-only updates, off-UI-thread work, and content-safe performance diagnostics part of the product contract.
The architecture and scope boundary are documented in the repository.
Future tasks preserve the service/UI ownership boundary.

tasks.title: Repository and Process-Boundary Foundation
tasks.goal: Create a locally validated open-source Rust workspace that proves the desktop/service boundary.

checks.text: Create workspace crates for protocol, service, terminal model, and desktop.
Add a versioned handshake and snapshot request over a Unix socket.
Add a seeded workspace/tab/pane state owned by the service.
Add a native desktop shell that reconnects and renders the snapshot structure.
Add license, contributing guidance, ignore rules, pinned toolchain, and CI.
Formatting passes.
Clippy passes with warnings denied.
Workspace tests pass.
A live service handshake and snapshot fetch are verified.

tasks.title: Persistent PTY Sessions
tasks.goal: Make the session service own real local and system-SSH shell processes and terminal byte streams.

checks.text: Add `portable-pty` behind a narrow service-owned Unix PTY abstraction on macOS and Linux.
Create, resize, write to, and terminate panes through explicit protocol commands.
Stream ordered output with bounded queues and reconnect-safe sequence numbers.
Keep every PTY draining into bounded daemon-owned history even when its desktop subscription is idle or disconnected.
Define graceful exit, forced termination, and service-shutdown semantics.
Prove that closing and reopening a client preserves the shell and its output.
Launch configured-host remote shells through system OpenSSH without bypassing SSH config, agents, host-key checks, or jump hosts.
Prove that desktop reconnect and pane movement preserve the OpenSSH PID and remote session identity.
Integration tests cover create/input/output/resize/exit.
A reconnect test proves the PTY survives desktop-client teardown.
Backpressure behavior is documented and tested.
A pane left unattended beyond the idle threshold cannot block its local or SSH child and can resume from a fresh snapshot without lost output.

tasks.title: Terminal Rendering and Input
tasks.goal: Render interactive terminal panes in the native desktop without duplicating terminal-emulation logic.

checks.text: Expand the `alacritty_terminal` adapter around parsing, resize, and visible-grid snapshots.
Add a GPUI terminal surface with monospaced text and HiDPI-aware PTY sizing.
Translate core keyboard and focus events into PTY input.
Add styled cells, cursor rendering, Unicode-width handling, IME, mouse reporting, and paste/clipboard integration.
Add scrollback, selection, copy, and search.
Add optional owner-only chunked terminal history with bounded non-blocking writes, visible gaps, lazy upward paging/search, and pause-without-deletion capacity defaults.
Keep terminal-model APIs independent of GPUI.
Move protocol decoding, terminal update preparation, and other non-paint work off the UI thread.
Render revision-aware deltas only for changed, actively subscribed panes and resync stale panes from one fresh snapshot on focus.
Interactive local shells render and accept input.
Unicode, colors, cursor modes, resize, and scrollback have regression coverage.
Desktop restart reconnects to the current rendered state.
Size and activity matrix measurements cover update volume, UI-thread work, resume latency, CPU, and memory for focused, recent, and stale panes.

tasks.title: Workspace and Pane Interactions
tasks.goal: Deliver the workspace, tab, split, and freely rearrangeable pane workflow.

checks.text: Implement create/rename/reorder/delete for workspaces and tabs.
Implement horizontal and vertical split-tree mutations.
Implement pane drag/drop with visible targets and cancel-safe behavior.
Persist layout changes atomically in the session service.
Restore focus and layout consistently after desktop restart.
Display and move local and SSH panes uniformly while retaining explicit connection state.
Add independent persisted terminal-accent and workspace-color defaults with explicit per-terminal and per-workspace overrides.
Every layout mutation has deterministic model tests.
Drag/drop works across splits and tabs without losing a local or SSH session.
Persisted layouts survive service and desktop restarts.
Appearance defaults and entity overrides survive desired-state migration and restart without changing PTY identity.

tasks.title: macOS Reliability Hardening
tasks.goal: Validate the reliability claim under desktop, display, daemon, and SSH lifecycle stress on macOS and Linux.

checks.text: Add structured service logs and opt-in diagnostics without recording terminal contents.
Add crash/reconnect, slow-client, high-output, and service-upgrade scenarios.
Define and measure idle-pane CPU, memory, serialized-byte, UI-thread, and focus-resume targets with diagnostics that never record terminal contents.
Test repeated Space switches, display attach/detach, sleep/wake, and fullscreen transitions.
Test Linux compositor/display-session changes and SSH network loss, host-key failure, jump-host, and desktop-reconnect behavior.
Add atomic state persistence and corruption recovery.
Package the service and desktop with clear start/stop/uninstall behavior.
Repeatable macOS and Linux soak tests run without UI freezes or lost local/SSH sessions.
Recovery behavior is documented for desktop crash, service crash, and corrupt state.
Release packaging preserves the independent service lifecycle.
Focused/recent panes remain responsive, stale panes stop generating live desktop traffic, and refocus performs one bounded fresh-snapshot resync before live deltas resume.
